Arabica grows slower at higher altitudes. That extra time on the branch builds natural sugars. When the bean is freeze-dried at low temperature, those sugars survive the process intact.

Spray drying uses hot air. The heat caramelizes the sugars into bitterness before they reach your cup.

Freeze-drying skips the heat. The frozen coffee goes straight from ice to vapor. The origin character — caramel, dark chocolate, bright acidity — stays in the granule.

Next morning, sip your black coffee before adding anything. Name the note you taste. That note is the altitude speaking.
